messages:
maya: Heads-up — saw a 2.5-3x tail latency spike on streaming jobs with long contexts (~50k tokens). Spikes line up with high evicter churn and sudden paging. Repro on staging: 10 concurrent streams -> one node hits 95% mem, pager activity, then 200–800ms extra per token.
trent: Can you paste the minimal repro and any profiler snapshots? quick confirmation needed if it's FIFO/LRU behavior or something else.
maya: Repro steps (staging):
1) start model server with KV hotset=0.6, reclaim-policy=fifo
2) run 10 streams with long-prefix (50k tokens) at 4 qps each
3) watch /metrics and `dmesg` for swap/pager logs

logs:
```
[t=2960004330] evicter: reclaim_iter start, target=512MB
[t=2960004334] pager: page-in stall 120ms, reclaimed=0
[t=2960004339] evicter: reinsert chain len=241 -> reorders observed
```
anya: From a quick `perf top` on the node it looked like evicter lock contention + lots of page faults. Top symbols:
```
  23%  evicter::reclaim
  18%  page_fault_handler
  12%  kv_store::reinsert
```
sam: Could be the reinsert-from-FIFO creating long chains when under bursty allocs. Two quick mitigations to try in staging: bump hotset watermark to 0.75 or switch reclaim-policy to `prob` for a run.
maya: Tried hotset=0.75 for 6h run — tail reduced from ~750ms -> ~320ms but still above baseline. Switching to `prob` cut tail to ~210ms.
trent: Interesting. Do we have any traces showing reinsert timestamps and ordering? That would show if we are incorrectly reusing entries or causing fragmentation.
maya: Uploaded a small pprof heap profile and a short trace to the internal bucket (link: https://internal/snapshots/296000/pprof). Key snippet shows many small allocations and repeated `reinsert` of same key IDs causing arena fragmentation.
anya: I dug into the code — FIFO path does a reinsert that acquires global bucket lock, then moves entries to tail even if they were recently accessed, causing thrash. Under paging this becomes linear chain work and causes page-ins inside the critical section.
sam: Proposal: make reinsert lock-free for hot recent accesses and add a per-bucket grace window to avoid reinsert for N ms. Minimal patch locally:
```
- if (reclaim_policy == FIFO) reinsert(entry);
+ if (reclaim_policy == FIFO && now - entry.last_access > REINSERT_GRACE_MS) reinsert(entry);
```
trent: Can you bench that patch? Also consider moving reinsert to a background, resumable task so page-faults don't block fast-path generation.
maya: Ran A/B with patch + grace=50ms: 10 streams, 6h run. Results: 95th tail down 46%, 99th down 62%. CPU slightly up (+4%) but overall better latency.
deploy-bot: Deployment: canary rolled to 3 nodes with patch 1f3b2a9 -> health OK -> monitoring for 2h.
anya: Next steps: add unit test asserting reinsert idempotency and add an integration test with synthetic pager pressure. Also add metric `evicter.reinsert_chain_length` to monitor.
trent: Good. Also add a note to ops runbook to prefer `prob` policy for very long-context streaming workloads until we get full fix in mainline.
maya: Filing a short postmortem and a perf ticket with traces and data. Thanks all :thumbsup:
